title_en: Heilongjiang Beidahuang Investment Guarantee Co., Ltd. v. Heilongjiang Province Jiansanjiang Agricultural Reclamation Qixing Grain, Oil, Industry and Trade Co., Ltd., Heilongjiang Province Jiansanjiang Agricultural Reclamation Hongda Grain, Oil, Industry and Trade Co., Ltd., et al. — dispute over guarantee contract
ruling_gist_en: Where a creditor's claim is secured by both a personal guarantee and a property guarantee provided by the debtor, and due to the joint fault of the creditor and the debtor, a pledge right that should have been established in accordance with the law fails to be established, and the guarantor has no fault in this regard, the creditor shall bear the adverse consequences of the non-establishment of the pledge right. Article 176 of the Property Law explicitly provides for the order of satisfaction of claims when property security provided by the debtor and personal security provided by a third party coexist. The guarantor has a reasonable reliance that the debtor's pledged property will be used first to satisfy the debt. If the creditor waives the pledge right, thereby impairing the guarantor's reliance interest in the order of priority, the guarantor shall, in accordance with Article 218 of the Property Law, be exempted from suretyship liability to the extent that the pledgee loses the right to priority of satisfaction.

full_text_en:
Heilongjiang Beidahuang Investment Guarantee Co., Ltd. v. Heilongjiang Jiansanjiang Agricultural Reclamation Qixing Grain and Oil Industry & Trade Co., Ltd., Heilongjiang Jiansanjiang Agricultural Reclamation Hongda Grain and Oil Industry & Trade Co., Ltd., et al. — dispute over guarantee contract

Ruling Summary

Where there is both a personal guarantee and a guarantee in kind provided by the debtor on the same creditor's right, and the common fault of the creditor and the debtor causes the pledge right which should have been established according to law not to be established, while the guarantor is not at fault for this, the creditor shall bear the adverse consequences of the non-establishment of the pledge right. Article 176 of the Property Law of the PRC expressly provides for the order of realization of the creditor's right when there is both a guarantee in kind provided by the debtor and a personal guarantee provided by a third party. The guarantor has a reasonable reliance interest that the creditor's right shall first be satisfied from the debtor's pledged property. The creditor's waiver of the pledge right impairs the guarantor's reliance interest in the order of priority. The guarantor shall, in accordance with Article 218 of the Property Law of the PRC, be exempted from the guarantee liability to the extent that the pledgee has lost the right to preferential satisfaction.

Civil Ruling of the Supreme People's Court

(2017) Supreme People's Court Civil Application No. 925

Re-applicant (plaintiff at first instance, appellant at second instance): Heilongjiang Beidahuang Investment Guarantee Co., Ltd., domiciled at Floors 27-28, Zhongrong International Building, No. 33 Songshan Road, Nangang District, Harbin City, Heilongjiang Province.

Legal representative: Wei Chenglin, General Manager of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Quan Lei, lawyer of Heilongjiang Shengdeli Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Wei Xiaoli, lawyer of Heilongjiang Shengdeli Law Firm.

Respondent (defendant at first instance, appellant at second instance): Heilongjiang Jiansanjiang Agricultural Reclamation Qixing Grain and Oil Industry & Trade Co., Ltd., domiciled at Jiansanjiang Tienan Development Zone, Fujin City, Jiamusi City, Heilongjiang Province.

Legal representative: Liu Xiben, General Manager of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Sun Peng, lawyer of Heilongjiang Meng Fanxu Law Firm.

Respondent (defendant at first instance, appellant at second instance): Heilongjiang Jiansanjiang Agricultural Reclamation Hongda Grain and Oil Industry & Trade Co., Ltd., domiciled at Block 13, Farm Headquarters, Qixing Farm, Fujin City, Jiamusi City, Heilongjiang Province.

Legal representative: Liu Xuefeng, Manager of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Sun Peng, lawyer of Heilongjiang Meng Fanxu Law Firm.

Respondent (defendant at first instance, appellant at second instance): Heilongjiang Jiansanjiang Agricultural Reclamation Hualong Grain and Oil Industry & Trade Co., Ltd., domiciled at Jiansanjiang Tienan Industrial Development Zone, Fujin City, Jiamusi City, Heilongjiang Province.

Legal representative: Liu Ziguang, Manager of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Sun Peng, lawyer of Heilongjiang Meng Fanxu Law Firm.

Respondent (defendant at first instance, appellant at second instance): Heilongjiang Jiansanjiang Agricultural Reclamation Daofu Rice Industry Co., Ltd., domiciled within the Thermal Power Plant of Jiansanjiang Branch, Fujin City, Jiamusi City, Heilongjiang Province.

Legal representative: Zhang Heguo, Manager of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Sun Peng, lawyer of Heilongjiang Meng Fanxu Law Firm.

Defendants at first instance: Heilongjiang Jiansanjiang Agricultural Reclamation Sanjiangyuan Rice Industry Co., Ltd., domiciled at No. 31, South Side of Jiafu Road, Tienanbei District, Fujin City, Heilongjiang Province.

Legal representative: Shao Shiling, Manager of the Company.

Defendant at first instance: Shao Shiling, female, born November 24, 1961, Han nationality, Manager of Heilongjiang Jiansanjiang Agricultural Reclamation Sanjiangyuan Rice Industry Co., Ltd., domiciled in Fujin City, Heilongjiang Province.

Defendant at first instance: Xu Yanjun, male, born July 3, 1962, Han nationality, shareholder of Heilongjiang Jiansanjiang Agricultural Reclamation Sanjiangyuan Rice Industry Co., Ltd., domiciled in Fujin City, Heilongjiang Province.

The re-applicant, Heilongjiang Beidahuang Investment Guarantee Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Beidahuang Guarantee Company), filed this application for retrial because of dissatisfaction with the civil judgment (2016) Hei Min Zhong No. 200 rendered by the High People's Court of Heilongjiang Province in the dispute over guarantee contract with the respondents, Heilongjiang Jiansanjiang Agricultural Reclamation Qixing Grain and Oil Industry & Trade Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Qixing Company), Heilongjiang Jiansanjiang Agricultural Reclamation Hongda Grain and Oil Industry & Trade Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Hongda Company), Heilongjiang Jiansanjiang Agricultural Reclamation Hualong Grain and Oil Industry & Trade Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Hualong Company), Heilongjiang Jiansanjiang Agricultural Reclamation Daofu Rice Industry Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Daofu Company), and the defendants at first instance, Heilongjiang Jiansanjiang Agricultural Reclamation Sanjiangyuan Rice Industry Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Sanjiangyuan Company), Shao Shiling, and Xu Yanjun. We formed a collegial panel in accordance with the law to review the case, and the review has now been concluded.

Beidahuang Guarantee Company filed an application for retrial alleging, among other things: (1) The court of second instance erred in determining the nature of the case. A guarantee contract is an ancillary contract, and the nature of the case cannot be determined based on the ancillary legal relationship. The guarantee company, after paying the debt on behalf of the debtor, seeks recourse against the borrower and the guarantors, not only based on the guarantee contract against the guarantor. Therefore, the court of first instance was correct in determining the nature of the case as a dispute over recourse, and the court of second instance erred in changing it to a dispute over guarantee contract. (2) The court of second instance's judgment exempting the four guarantors from liability within the value of the 4,560 tons of rice involved in the case lacks factual and legal basis. Xu Yanjun testified that Shao Shiling sold the pledged rice, indicating that the actual control of the 4,560 tons of rice was with Sanjiangyuan Company and was not delivered to Beidahuang Guarantee Company. Delivery of the pledged property is a condition for the establishment of a pledge right or the entry into effect of a pledge contract. Therefore, the rice pledge contract relationship established between Beidahuang Guarantee Company and Sanjiangyuan Company was formed but did not take effect. The four guarantors should bear joint and several guarantee liability for the loan debt involved in the case, and the court of second instance erred in not correcting this. Sanjiangyuan Company, Qixing Company, Hualong Company, and Daofu Company did not go through the formalities of pledging rice, nor did they provide rice as security to Beidahuang Guarantee Company. Only after Hongda Company provided sufficient rice did Beidahuang Guarantee Company go through the rice pledge formalities with that company. Although the several companies had a joint guarantee relationship, the forms of counter-guarantee were different. The "Notice Letter" issued by Beidahuang Guarantee Company to Hongda Company is insufficient to prove that the four guarantors had a reasonable reliance on the rice guarantee provided by Sanjiangyuan Company. The guarantee contracts signed between Beidahuang Guarantee Company and the four guarantors did not stipulate the pledge of rice or any other security in kind. The four guarantors were not aware of Sanjiangyuan's rice pledge, nor did they provide the guarantee because of Sanjiangyuan's rice pledge. The so-called "reasonable reliance" imposed by the court of second instance is a subjective and erroneous finding. (3) The court of second instance's determination that the value of the 4,560 tons of rice involved in the case was RMB 14,136,000 is without factual or legal basis. The pledge guarantee contract signed between Sanjiangyuan Company and Beidahuang Guarantee Company stipulated a pledge rate of 70% for the 4,560 tons of rice. Even if the pledge right had been established, the value of the pledge guarantee would have been only over RMB 8 million. In summary, Beidahuang Guarantee Company applied for retrial pursuant to Item 1 and Item 2 of Article 200 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC.

Qixing Company, Hongda Company, Hualong Company, and Daofu Company submitted their opinions, stating that Beidahuang Guarantee Company's application for retrial lacks factual and legal basis and should be dismissed.

During our review, Beidahuang Guarantee Company submitted two new pieces of evidence: Evidence One, a "Statement of Facts" issued by Xu Yanjun, intended to prove that Shao Shiling, the legal representative of Sanjiangyuan Company, and Liu Ziguang, the legal representative of Hualong Company, maliciously colluded to sell the 4,560 tons of rice, the subject matter of the pledge involved in the case, resulting in Beidahuang Guarantee Company's inability to recover the loan loss; Evidence Two, photographs of the business premises of Sanjiangyuan Company, intended to prove that the equipment and factory buildings mortgaged by Sanjiangyuan Company to Beidahuang Guarantee Company were dilapidated and could not compensate for its losses.

Qixing Company, Hongda Company, Hualong Company, and Daofu Company argued during cross-examination that the authenticity of Evidence One could not be confirmed, and the so-called "Statement of Facts" of Xu Yanjun contradicted his own statements in the first and second instance proceedings of this case, and was not relevant to whether the guarantors should bear guarantee liability. Evidence Two could only reflect the current status of Sanjiangyuan Company and had no relevance to the purpose Beidahuang Guarantee Company sought to prove. In summary, the above evidence did not constitute new evidence sufficient to overturn the original judgment.

We certify as follows: Xu Yanjun, as a party to this case, the "Statement of Facts" he issued constitutes a statement of a party. Since he did not participate in the inquiry and the evidence was a copy, its authenticity cannot be confirmed, so we do not accept it. Evidence Two is irrelevant to the purpose Beidahuang Guarantee Company sought to prove. In summary, the above two pieces of evidence do not constitute new evidence sufficient to overturn the original judgment, and we do not accept them.

Upon review, we find:

(1) Regarding whether the nature of the case should be a dispute over recourse or a dispute over guarantee contract

The nature of a civil case should be determined based on the nature of the legal relationship claimed by the parties. If more than two legal relationships are involved in the same lawsuit, the nature of the case should be determined based on the nature of the legal relationship in dispute between the parties. If both are legal relationships in dispute, then two parallel case natures should be determined based on the two or more legal relationships in dispute. There are multiple legal relationships in this case: The primary legal relationship is the loan contract relationship between Sanjiangyuan Company and China Construction Bank Corporation Harbin Agricultural Reclamation Sub-branch (hereinafter referred to as Agricultural Reclamation CCB); the ancillary legal relationship is the guarantee contract relationship between Beidahuang Guarantee Company and Agricultural Reclamation CCB, whereby Beidahuang Guarantee Company provided joint and several liability guarantee for the above loan; at the same time, this case also involves a counter-guarantee contract relationship, i.e., the debtor Sanjiangyuan Company provided a counter-guarantee to Beidahuang Guarantee Company by way of mortgage of machinery and equipment and pledge of 4,560 tons of rice, the legal representative of Sanjiangyuan Company, Shao Shiling, and her spouse Xu Yanjun provided a counter-guarantee by way of mortgage of real estate and pledge of equity, and Qixing Company, Hongda Company, Hualong Company, and Daofu Company provided joint and several liability guarantee to Beidahuang Guarantee Company within the scope of the RMB 10 million loan. This case is a lawsuit in which Beidahuang Guarantee Company, as the joint and several guarantor of the principal debt, after paying off Sanjiangyuan Company's loan debt on its behalf, seeks recourse against the debtor Sanjiangyuan Company for the amount paid based on its statutory right of recourse, and seeks counter-guarantee liability against the counter-guarantors based on the counter-guarantee contract relationship. Therefore, the nature of the case should be determined as a dispute over recourse and a dispute over guarantee contract. The court of first instance determined the nature of the case as a dispute over recourse, and the court of second instance adjusted it to a dispute over guarantee contract. Neither determination was complete. However, since both the court of first instance and the court of second instance heard the legal relationships in dispute in this case, the defect in the determination of the nature of the case did not affect the substantive trial of the case. Therefore, this issue is insufficient to warrant a retrial of this case.

(2) Regarding whether, when the pledge provided by the debtor was not established, the guarantors should be exempted from joint and several guarantee liability to the extent of the priority compensation of the pledged property

In this case, the pledge contract, mortgage contract, and guarantee contracts signed on the same day between Beidahuang Guarantee Company and the debtor and third parties respectively were all true expressions of the parties' intentions, did not violate the mandatory provisions of laws and administrative regulations, and should be legally recognized as valid contracts. Among them, although the rice pledge contract signed between Beidahuang Guarantee Company and the debtor Sanjiangyuan Company was lawfully formed and became effective, since Sanjiangyuan Company did not deliver the pledged property and sold the pledged rice to an outsider, in accordance with the provision of Article 212 of the Property Law of the PRC that "the pledge right is established when the pledgor delivers the pledged property to the pledgee," it should be determined that Beidahuang Guarantee Company's rice pledge right was not established. What impact the non-establishment of the pledge right has on the guarantors' guarantee liability, and whether the guarantors should be exempted from guarantee liability to the extent of the priority compensation of the pledged property, is the core dispute between the parties in this case. On this issue, the findings of the court of first instance and the court of second instance differed. The court of first instance ordered the four guarantors to bear joint and several guarantee liability within 50% of the value of the unestablished pledge right, while the court of second instance modified the judgment to exempt the four guarantors from guarantee liability within the value of the 4,560 tons of rice, the subject matter of the pledge involved in the case. We find that, taking all the facts of the case into consideration, the court of second instance's determination exempting the guarantors is not improper, for the following reasons:

First, Beidahuang Guarantee Company and Sanjiangyuan Company failed to honestly and creditably actively perform the obligations under the effective pledge contract. Both parties were at fault for the non-establishment of the pledge right, causing the pledge right that should have been effectively established to fail to function as a guarantee in kind, and the at-fault parties should bear the adverse consequences. After the pledge contract involved was signed, Sanjiangyuan Company did not deliver the pledged 4,560 tons of rice to Beidahuang Guarantee Company, but stored the pledged property in its own warehouse. Subsequently, it privately sold the pledged property to an outsider and did not use the proceeds from the sale to repay the debt, showing subjective malice in evading debt and shifting the repayment responsibility to other guarantors. The company was at fault for the non-establishment of the pledge right. Beidahuang Guarantee Company, as a professional guarantee company and the counter-guarantee creditor, should have been aware of the commercial risks and legal consequences of the pledgor's failure to deliver the pledged property, as well as the impact of such conduct on the interests of the guarantors of the same creditor's right. Moreover, the pledged rice is a grain crop, difficult to store for a long time, and subject to possible disposal by the debtor. The company should have exercised due care and attention. However, after signing the pledge contract, the company never requested Sanjiangyuan Company to deliver the pledged property. Even if the rice was stored in Sanjiangyuan Company's warehouse for the convenience of storage, Beidahuang Guarantee Company should have exercised supervision over the pledged property to keep it under its control, but it neglected supervision, allowing the debtor to privately dispose of the pledged property. After learning that the pledged property was sold to a specific outsider, "Sinograin," Beidahuang Guarantee Company did not actively demand that Sanjiangyuan Company use the proceeds from the sale to repay the debt to mitigate damages, but instead "slept on its rights" because there were multiple guarantees on its credit. This is clearly a violation of good faith. Therefore, the common fault of the creditor and the debtor caused the pledge right that should have been established according to law to fail to function as a guarantee in kind, and the guarantors were not at fault for this. Beidahuang Guarantee Company should bear the adverse consequences of its passive conduct in failing to safeguard the interests of its credit.

Second, although the guarantee contracts did not expressly stipulate that the debtor's provision of the rice pledge was a condition for the guarantors to provide the guarantee, the Property Law of the PRC has clear provisions on the order of realization of the creditor's right when there is both a guarantee in kind provided by the debtor and a personal guarantee provided by a third party. The guarantors had a reasonable reliance interest that the creditor's right would be first satisfied from the debtor's pledged property. Beidahuang Guarantee Company's failure to exercise its right to demand delivery of the pledged property impaired the guarantors' reliance interest in the order of priority. The guarantors should be exempted from liability to the extent of the value of the priority compensation of the pledged property. In this case, the loan debtor Sanjiangyuan Company and the four guarantors were all rice processing enterprises, and there was a relationship of joint guarantee among the five households, with the same form of joint guarantee. That is, the bank loans of any one household were guaranteed by Beidahuang Guarantee Company, and then the loan debtor provided mortgage and pledge guarantees to Beidahuang Guarantee Company with its own machinery, equipment, real estate, and rice, while the other four households provided guarantee guarantees to Beidahuang Guarantee Company. The pledge contract and guarantee contracts involved were signed on the same day. The above facts show that all parties involved were aware that Beidahuang Guarantee Company's counter-guarantee credit should have been secured by both a guarantee in kind provided by the debtor and a personal guarantee provided by a third party. Article 176 of the Property Law of the PRC provides: "If a guaranteed claim is secured by both a security interest in property and a suretyship, and the debtor defaults on its debt or the parties agree on the circumstances for realizing the security interest, the creditor shall realize the claim in accordance with the agreement. If there is no agreement or the agreement is unclear, and the debtor himself provides the security interest in property, the creditor shall first realize the claim against the security interest in property. If a third party provides the security interest in property, the creditor may realize the claim against the security interest in property or require the surety to bear the suretyship liability. After a third party providing the security bears the suretyship liability, he is entitled to seek recourse against the debtor." According to the above provisions, since the parties in this case did not agree on the order of realization of the creditor's right, if the security interest in property provided by the debtor had been normally established, the guarantors would only bear guarantee liability for the part of the creditor's right not covered by the security interest in property. Therefore, the four guarantors had a reasonable reliance on their statutory right of priority. The fact that the legal representative of Qixing Company, Liu Xiben, and the legal representative of Hongda Company, Liu Xuefeng, immediately reported to the public security department after learning that Sanjiangyuan Company had disposed of the pledged property also proves the existence of such reliance by the guarantors. The reliance interest arising therefrom is protected by law. If the guarantors were ordered to continue to bear guarantee liability when the security interest in property provided by the debtor was not established, the interests of the maliciously breaching debtor and the creditor who failed to exercise its rights would not be harmed, but the guarantors' reliance interest would be infringed. This would undoubtedly violate the principles of fairness and good faith in civil law.

Based on the above two aspects of analysis, the guarantors' reasonable reliance interest in the order of priority was harmed by the creditor and the debtor. The guarantors should be exempted from guarantee liability within the value of the 4,560 tons of rice, which is the subject matter of the pledge.

(3) Regarding how the value of the 4,560 tons of rice (the subject matter of the pledge), i.e., the scope of exemption of the four guarantors, should be determined

If the pledge right had been established, the pledgee's creditor's right, if not satisfied, should be satisfied on a priority basis from the proceeds of the auction or sale of the pledged property. Since Beidahuang Guarantee Company's pledge right was not established in this case, the court of second instance, based on the guidance price in the "Notice on the Policy of Purchase Price and Quality for Minimum Purchase Price Acquisition of Rice in 2014" (Hei Liang Nong Lian [2014] No. 102) issued jointly by the Grain Bureau of Heilongjiang Province, the Heilongjiang Branch of China Grain Reserves Corporation, and the Heilongjiang Branch of the Agricultural Development Bank of China, which set the minimum purchase price for rice in 2014 at RMB 1.55 per jin (0.5 kg), determined the value of the 4,560 tons of rice involved to be RMB 14,136,000. This determination has a clear basis and is not improper. Considering that Sanjiangyuan Company's proceeds from selling the above pledged property were over RMB 13 million, and the disputed creditor's right amount is RMB 10 million, the court of second instance's judgment exempting the four guarantors from guarantee liability is not improper.

In summary, Beidahuang Guarantee Company's application for retrial does not meet the circumstances specified in Items 1 and 2 of Article 200 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC. In accordance with Article 204, Paragraph 1 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC and Article 395, Paragraph 2 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, we rule as follows:

The application for retrial filed by Heilongjiang Beidahuang Investment Guarantee Co., Ltd. is dismissed.

Presiding Judge: Pan Jie

Judge: Luo Dian

Judge: Wan Ting

July 17, 2017
